title: X posts from Quantic's data: an experiment, measured
body:
An experiment, not a milestone: can the 27B write short X posts from Quantic's public data, and can it check them? Only `docs/` changes: [`docs/benchmarks/2026-10-28-x-posts/`](https://github.com/fleveque/quantic-agent/blob/x-posts/docs/benchmarks/2026-10-28-x-posts/README.md) and a row in the benchmarks index. The scripts were throwaway (built on `quantic.Server`, `llm.Client`, `provenance`, `wording`, `xpost.x_length`); the data, every post, the blind labels, the verdicts and every prompt verbatim are kept.

## Findings

- **Code gathers, the model writes.** Given the tools, the 27B made 6 calls and wrote lists of facts. Given facts computed by code, it wrote varied posts with every figure traced.
- **Field meanings fixed most errors at the source.** Wrong claims went from 19 of 95 posts to 2 of 96 once the writer was told what each field means (`seen_on` read as the date of the change was 6 of 11 major errors).
- **A 27B verifier** caught 9 of 11 major errors given the post's own facts (10 of 73 correct posts flagged), and none given all the facts. Two things changed between those runs, so they can't be separated.
- **Links chosen by code** went to the wrong company in 3 posts, because the model cited the wrong fact ids and figures were traced to every fact rather than the post's own. Tracing them to the cited facts, and requiring each cited company to be named, fixed it. The Week Ahead's provenance traces figures to the whole run in the same way.
- **One company, catchier (Nike):** asked to be punchy, the 27B wrote lists of fragments; asked to write like a person, prose. Four checks made posts worse ("Best Buy" read as advice, also in `wording.py` on `main`; "price" banned; a threshold inside a string; a term that let a wrong figure through). Fixed, 5 of 14 passing versions still had a claim no check sees ("pays its next dividend in March", a streak "that started in 2014").
- **The data, for Quantic:** streaks stop at 29 years (the Dividend Kings list returns 29 and 12), rounding is recorded as cuts (10 of 14 in 30 days were under 1%), deep cuts are labelled safe, and listings of the same company disagree.

Blind labels are mine (Claude), one labeller; the posts repeat the same 55 facts.

## Checks

`ruff format --check`, `ruff check`, `pyright` (strict), `pytest` (448 passed), and the relative-link check, all run locally on b6cf062 and d3c4380; CI green on both.
